signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry
signals.text: AUD/CHF trades at 0.5807 against a backdrop where AUD leads G10 performance at +0.785% across 4 pairs while CHF lags at -0.430% across 6 pairs, generating a 1.215% bilateral spread. The 2s10s curve sits in a bull flattener regime with 3m10s at +123.2bp, while the rate differential anchored by AONIA at 4.60% versus SARON at -0.04% provides a +460bp carry advantage supporting the base currency. Retail sentiment data retail sentiment shows a 78% short bias in AUD/CHF, establishing a pronounced positioning divergence against institutional longs. Trade bias: Long AUD/CHF; wide carry differential supports continued outperformance. Catalyst: Reserve Bank of Australia meeting 3 Nov — hold expected at 4.60%. Risk: G10 spread compresses below 0.80% as risk-off flows compress cross-currency yield differentials.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Positioning + Options Skew + Carry
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.37, positioned above its SMA20 at 156.64 and SMA50 at 157.79 while remaining below the SMA200 at 158.50. CFTC speculative positioning shows JPY net short -16,809 contracts with the 52-week percentile at 96 and z-score at +1.83σ, confirming an extreme and crowded short base. The 25-day risk reversal prints at -2.01, showing strong put skew and elevated hedging demand for downside protection as the options market braces for volatility. The OIS overnight benchmark rate differential between SOFR at 3.89% and TONA at 1.23% provides a +266bp carry advantage favoring the dollar. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY; crowded speculative shorts and wide carry support the pair despite options hedging. Catalyst: US 10-Year Note Auction at 17:00 UTC. Risk: VIX breaks above 25, sparking a disorderly carry unwind that overwhelms the yield differential.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Retail Extreme Divergence + Carry
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.4221, holding above its SMA20 at 1.4063, SMA50 at 1.3964, and SMA200 at 1.3860. The 25-day risk reversal sits at +0.30, reflecting a mild call skew in the options market while Retail sentiment data retail sentiment shows an extreme 96% short bias, creating a stark contrarian divergence. The OIS overnight rate differential between SOFR at 3.89% and CORRA at 2.29% maintains a +160bp carry advantage favoring the dollar. Economic Surprise Index data for Canada shows an index of +15.1, signaling sustained positive data beats against expectations. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD; positive rate differential and retail short extreme support the pair. Catalyst: BoC meeting 28 Oct — hold expected at 2.25%. Risk: Canadian economic data continues to beat expectations and forces retail short capitulation.
